title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
annotation: A witty portrait of manners and marriage in Regency England, centered on the sharp-tongued Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr. Darcy.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Bronte
annotation: A dark, obsessive love story set on the Yorkshire moors, following the destructive bond between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Bronte
annotation: An orphaned governess navigates hardship, love, and independence in a story of moral resilience and self-respect.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
annotation: A young orphan named Pip rises through unexpected wealth while confronting the true cost of ambition and class.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
annotation: An orphan boy escapes a workhouse into London's criminal underworld, exposing Victorian poverty and cruelty.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
annotation: A Transylvanian count travels to England, unleashing terror as a group of Victorians race to stop his spreading curse.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
annotation: A scientist's creation of life leads to tragedy, exploring ambition, isolation, and the consequences of playing god.

title: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
annotation: A respectable doctor's secret experiment unleashes a violent alter ego, probing the duality of human nature.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
annotation: Sherlock Holmes investigates a legendary curse and a spectral hound terrorizing an aristocratic family on the moors.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
annotation: The first meeting of Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson, unraveling a murder tied to a decades-old revenge plot.

title: The Turn of the Screw
author: Henry James
annotation: A governess grows convinced that malevolent ghosts are threatening the two children in her care.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
annotation: A young bride is haunted by the lingering presence of her husband's first wife in a gothic Cornish mansion.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
annotation: Ten strangers are lured to an isolated island and killed one by one according to an ominous nursery rhyme.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
annotation: Detective Hercule Poirot must solve a murder aboard a snowbound train filled with suspects hiding secrets.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
annotation: A man stays eternally youthful while his portrait absorbs the moral decay of his hedonistic life.

author: George Orwell
annotation: In a totalitarian surveillance state, a man's quiet rebellion against the Party leads to devastating consequences.

title: Vanity Fair
author: William Thackeray
annotation: A satirical chronicle of social climbing and ambition, following the cunning Becky Sharp through English society.

title: Middlemarch
author: George Eliot
annotation: Interwoven lives in a provincial English town explore marriage, idealism, and disappointed ambition.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H.G. Wells
annotation: A Martian invasion devastates England, told through one man's harrowing account of survival and terror.

title: Wuthering Heights (annotated)
author: Emily Bronte
annotation: A study edition of the classic tale of doomed love and vengeance on the English moors.

title: Les Miserables
author: Victor Hugo
annotation: An ex-convict seeks redemption while pursued by a relentless inspector against the backdrop of revolutionary France.

title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame
author: Victor Hugo
annotation: A deformed bell-ringer and a gypsy dancer become entangled in tragedy amid medieval Paris.

title: Madame Bovary
author: Gustave Flaubert
annotation: A provincial doctor's wife pursues romantic fantasies that lead to ruin and despair.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
annotation: An innocent man escapes wrongful imprisonment and returns under a new identity to enact an elaborate revenge.

title: The Three Musketeers
author: Alexandre Dumas
annotation: A young swordsman joins three legendary musketeers in court intrigue and daring adventure in 17th-century France.

title: Le Pere Goriot
author: Honore de Balzac
annotation: An aging father's devotion to his ungrateful daughters unfolds alongside a young man's moral corruption in Paris.

title: The Phantom of the Opera
author: Gaston Leroux
annotation: A disfigured musical genius haunts the Paris Opera House, obsessed with a young singer.

title: Therese Raquin
author: Emile Zola
annotation: A woman and her lover are consumed by guilt after murdering her husband, unraveling under psychological torment.

title: Germinal
author: Emile Zola
annotation: A brutal strike among French coal miners exposes class struggle and the human cost of industrial exploitation.

title: The Stranger
author: Albert Camus
annotation: A detached man's indifferent reaction to his mother's death and a subsequent killing explores absurdist philosophy.

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
annotation: A professor and his companions descend through a volcanic passage into a fantastical subterranean world.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
annotation: Captain Nemo pilots the submarine Nautilus through underwater wonders and dangers unknown to the surface world.

title: Bel-Ami
author: Guy de Maupassant
annotation: An ambitious former soldier claws his way up Parisian society through manipulation and seduction.

title: The Necklace and Other Stories
author: Guy de Maupassant
annotation: A collection of sharp, ironic tales about vanity, deception, and the fragility of social status.

title: Nana
author: Emile Zola
annotation: A courtesan's rise through Parisian theater and high society exposes the decadence and hypocrisy beneath it.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
annotation: A destitute former student commits murder to test his own theory of moral exceptionalism, then unravels under guilt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
annotation: Three brothers and their depraved father collide in a story of faith, doubt, and patricide in provincial Russia.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
annotation: Sweeping across the Napoleonic Wars, aristocratic families navigate love, loss, and the tides of history.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
annotation: A married aristocrat's passionate affair leads to social ruin, set against another character's quiet search for meaning.

title: Dead Souls
author: Nikolai Gogol
annotation: A con man travels the Russian countryside buying the records of deceased serfs in a satirical scheme.

title: The Overcoat
author: Nikolai Gogol
annotation: A poor clerk's prized new coat brings him fleeting dignity before tragedy strikes in this satire of bureaucracy.

title: Fathers and Sons
author: Ivan Turgenev
annotation: A young nihilist's return home ignites generational conflict over tradition, science, and belief.

title: The Master and Margarita
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
annotation: The Devil visits Soviet Moscow, unleashing chaos that intertwines with a suppressed novel about Pontius Pilate.

title: Eugene Onegin
author: Alexander Pushkin
annotation: A jaded aristocrat rejects a young woman's love, only to face devastating regret years later.

title: The Queen of Spades
author: Alexander Pushkin
annotation: An officer's obsession with an old countess's secret gambling formula spirals into madness and ruin.

title: Viy
author: Nikolai Gogol
annotation: A young seminarian is tormented by supernatural horrors while praying over the body of a mysterious witch.

title: The Idiot
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
annotation: A guileless, kind-hearted prince returns to Russian society and is nearly destroyed by its cynicism and greed.

title: Demons
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
annotation: A group of revolutionaries' nihilistic plotting brings chaos and tragedy to a provincial Russian town.

title: Notes from Underground
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
annotation: A bitter, isolated narrator's rambling confessions dissect free will, spite, and alienation.

title: A Hero of Our Time
author: Mikhail Lermontov
annotation: A cynical, self-destructive officer's adventures in the Caucasus reveal the disillusionment of his generation.
